title: Editorial anomaly re "blocked by a modal dialog"

labels.name: editorial
labels.description: Changes that do not affect how the standard is understood

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

In the [show a modal dialog](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#show-a-modal-dialog) algorithm, step 14 says:
> Set subject's [node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document) to be [blocked by the modal dialog](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#blocked-by-a-modal-dialog) subject.

But "blocked by a modal dialog" is defined as a relation in the data model. So the only way to make a document be blocked by a modal dialog is to change the data model, which the spec would normally do explicitly.

(Before PR #11336, the step in question used "Let" rather than "Set", but the problem is the same.)

Note that step **15** does change the data model, but I'm not sure if it's guaranteed to cause  the definition of "blocked by a modal dialog" to be satisfied.

History: Once upon a time, "blocked by a modal dialog" was just a marking that could be applied to a document, so it made sense that an algo step could simply say that a document was now blocked by a modal dialog, and that would accomplish the marking. The change in the definition happened in 2017, in ea14be5f (line 72335/72294). At that time, step 14 in "show a modal dialog" should probably have been changed, but it wasn't.  Step 15 was inserted, so maybe it should have *replaced* step 14.
